how_used.manning_n: Cell n = area-weighted mean of the class n over the 10 m pixels inside the 30 m model cell. Face n = mean of its two cells (as SFINCS).
how_used.curve_number: Cell CN = area-weighted mean of the class CN for the cell's hydrologic soil group (NRCS TR-55 composite CN; built-area pixels count as directly connected impervious surface, CN 98). Antecedent runoff condition II (average).

sources.n: HEC-RAS 2D land-classification table after Chow (1959); see data/roughness/worldcover-manning.json for the per-class reasoning (same physical classes).
sources.cn: USDA NRCS (1986) Urban Hydrology for Small Watersheds, TR-55, Tables 2-2a to 2-2c.
sources.hsg: Hydrologic soil group from SoilGrids 2.0 sand and clay (0-100 cm, depth-weighted) with the texture criteria of USDA NRCS (2009) NEH Part 630 Chapter 7, as used for HYSOGs250m (Ross et al. 2018).

1.label: Water
1.cn_basis: Open water: all rain becomes runoff (no infiltration).

2.label: Trees
2.cn_basis: TR-55 Table 2-2c, woods, good hydrologic condition.

4.label: Flooded vegetation
4.cn_basis: Saturated surface: treated like an impervious surface (TR-55 CN 98).

5.label: Crops
5.cn_basis: TR-55 Table 2-2b, row crops, straight row, good condition.

7.label: Built area
7.cn_basis: IO defines built area as human-made structures, roads and impervious surfaces: TR-55 Table 2-2a impervious areas (roofs, paved), CN 98.

8.label: Bare ground
8.cn_basis: TR-55 Table 2-2a, newly graded areas (pervious, no vegetation).

11.label: Rangeland
11.cn_basis: TR-55 Table 2-2c, pasture, grassland or range, fair condition.

unclassified_rule: Pixels with no class or class 10 (clouds) take the mean of the classified pixels in the same cell; a cell with none takes built area (the dominant class of the region).

hsg_rule.B: clay 10-20 % and sand 50-90 %, or clay < 10 % and sand <= 90 % with sand >= 50 %
hsg_rule.C: clay 20-40 %, or clay < 20 % and sand < 50 % (loam, silt loam, silt)
